data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew language, Amasa means 'beloved'. In the Bible, there is a character named Amasa who was a commander of the army under King David. The name Amasa carries the meaning “Beloved” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Amasa usually hope their child will grow to embody beloved and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Amasa belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Beloved.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Amasa total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

It is known from various sources in the Bible - 2 Samuel 16:5, 20: 'And Saul cried to God, saying, Bring me back the man in whose hand this spear is, and I will give you two hundred shekels of silver. And Abishai the son of Zeruiah said, Why should this dead dog curse me with his tongue? Therefore, let me go to him and take away the spear from his hand.' - 2 Samuel 20: 'And Jonathan said to David, Go in peace, forasmuch as we have sworn both of us in the name of the Lord, saying, The Lord shall be between me and thee, and between my seed and thy seed for ever.' - 2 Samuel 16: Amasa is a name that appears in the Bible as a name of strength, power, or labor. The name Amasa comes from the Hebrew word 'amasa', which means 'to bear or carry'. In Christian tradition, the name Amasa represents a man of great strength, power, and labor. In modern usage, the name Amasa is used in various cultures and contexts, often symbolizing strength, power, or labor.
